name: Lamb Tavern Leadenhall
description: A Leadenhall Market Victorian pub (1780) — old mahogany, etched glass, and a City crowd after work.

name: Nag's Head Covent Garden
description: McMullen's tiny pub tucked behind Covent Garden — unreformed, tile-bar, a theatre district gem.

name: The Luggage Room
description: A Marylebone Georgian-themed speakeasy — discreet entrance, 1920s cocktails, live jazz on weekends.

name: Nutbourne
description: A Battersea wine bar-restaurant — English wines from the family's own Nutbourne vineyard, modern British cooking.

name: Pantechnicon
description: Belgravia Japanese-Scandinavian fusion — a sunlit rooftop bar, top-floor cocktail terrace, and Eldr restaurant on ground floor.

name: Rotunda Bar King's Cross
description: The Rotunda bar at Kings Place — riverside terrace overlooking Battlebridge Basin, ideal before a Kings Place concert.

name: The Spread Eagle Camden
description: A large Camden pub with a Victorian exterior — live rock music at the back room, ordinary pub up front.

name: The Crown Greenwich
description: A traditional pub a block from Greenwich Market — cask ales and Fuller's London Pride, a proper neighbourhood local.

name: The Old Brewery Greenwich
description: A working microbrewery and pub in the Old Royal Naval College — Meantime Brewing's on-site microbrewery.
address: Pepys Building, Old Royal Naval College, London SE10 9LW

name: Coach & Horses Bruton Street
description: Mayfair Bruton Street pub dating to 1744 — wood-panelled, atmospheric, a rare gem on Mayfair's art-dealer street.
tips: Gets busy at 5pm with City-to-Mayfair crowd.

name: Scarfes Bar at Rosewood London
description: The cocktail bar at the Rosewood London — Gerald Scarfe-illustrated walls, live jazz, whisky tastings.

name: Lyle Bar at Lyle's
description: Upstairs bar of Michelin-starred Lyle's — natural wines, fermented kombuchas, creative non-alcoholic cocktails.
address: Tea Building, 56 Shoreditch High St, London E1 6JJ

name: Bar Brosé
description: Covent Garden basement wine-bar — £22 'rosé all day' menu, natural-wine forward list.

name: Discount Suit Company
description: Liverpool Street basement — originally a suit-warehouse turned speakeasy, with curious décor and serious cocktails.

name: Lab E20
description: Westfield Stratford City cocktail bar — rotating residencies, buzzing after-shopping destination.

name: The Lucky Pig
description: A tiny Piccadilly speakeasy — just 30 seats, and a whisky-forward menu. Discreet entrance.
tips: Follow the sign for 'Oxford Circus Underground' — the bar is behind.

name: The Marksman
description: Hackney Road gastropub — 19th-century exterior, Michelin Bib Gourmand-approved cooking, pub at its finest.
tips: Book for restaurant. Walk-in for bar.

name: The Duke of Sussex
description: Chiswick gastropub with a year-round garden — Spanish-leaning menu, seasonal tapas, a sharp wine list.

name: Draft House
description: A beer-pub chain focused on craft beer — rotating casks, tasting flights, American-style food.
tips: Multiple branches. Good for introducing craft to the beer-curious.

name: The Bridge House
description: A London-Bridge-adjacent pub — 17th-century building, unreformed since the Georgians, a cornerstone.
tips: Sunday roast is a South-London classic.

name: The Crown & Anchor Brixton
description: Brixton's craft-beer community pub — 20+ taps, regular events, a strong local following.

name: The Ship Wandsworth
description: Wandsworth riverside pub with a beer garden — Fuller's pub, Thames-side terrace, a destination for summer drinks.

name: The Bell Aldgate
description: An Aldgate pub above the East End's oldest crossroads — history meets budget pints, near the former city gate.

name: Butler's Wharf Chop House
description: A riverside D&D pub-restaurant with Tower Bridge views — British menu, pub downstairs, terrace dining upstairs.

name: The Anchor & Hope Kingsland
description: Waterloo gastropub (distinct from The Anchor Bankside) — no-reservations, daily-changing menu, a cornerstone of the London dining scene.
tips: Queue for dinner; Sunday lunch seating 2pm bookable.

name: Fox & Anchor
description: A Smithfield pub open from 7am for 'market breakfasts' — traditional pub, serious breakfasts with ale on the side.
tips: 'City Boy' breakfast: bacon, eggs, black pudding, half pint of Guinness.

name: The Lockhouse
description: A converted East End lock-keeper's cottage turned pub — tiny, photogenic, riverside.
tips: Check exact location online — area developing.

name: The Dog & Wardrobe
description: A Dalston pub — unreformed, community-first, great cask ale selection.

name: The Prince of Wales Putney
description: Putney's riverside Fuller's pub — Boat-Race viewing point, large terrace, pie-and-pint menu.
tips: Boat Race day (late March/early April) a London ritual.

name: The Elms
description: A Dulwich pub — wood-floored, dog-friendly, real fire in winter.

name: Peckham Palms
description: A roof-terrace bar at the Aylesham Centre — summer-only, Caribbean-spirit cocktails, a Peckham weekend hit.
tips: Summer only. Tickets for some events.

name: Native at Browns
description: Browns Hotel's tiny natural-wine and seasonal-food bar — low-ceilinged, candle-lit, honest cooking.

name: Happiness Forgets Worship Street
description: The Worship Street sibling to Happiness Forgets — similar minimalism, different crowd.
